articleTitle: Modeling and computing of random lasing dynamics
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Dynamics of random lasing (RL) is computed using Monte-Carlo simulation. Three stages of RL formation were searched out: accumulation of pump photons and excited molecules in the sample; formation of multiple-modes RL (II); relaxation of RL radiations with preferential preservation of high-Q modes (III). The dominate role of high-Q modes in RL formation are pointed at.

articleTitle: Fractional electromagnetic waves
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: In The present work we consider the electromagnetic wave equation in terms of the fractional derivative of the Caputo type. The order of the derivative being considered is 0<;λ≤1. A new parameter σ is introduced which characterizes the existence of the fractional components in the system. We analyze fractional derivative with respect to time and space for γ=1 and 1/2.

articleTitle: Thresholds of lasing and modal patterns of a limacon cavity analysed with Muller's integral equations
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We consider the lasing characteristics of the natural modes in a limacon active microcavity. The modes are the solutions to the two-dimensional (2-D) linear eigenproblem for the Maxwell equations with exact boundary conditions and radiation condition at infinity. This problem is reduced equivalently to the set of Muller's integral equations of the Fredholm second kind and discretized using the exponentially convergent quadrature formulas. The numerical studies of lasing thresholds and modal field patterns of the whispering-gallery modes are presented. They demonstrate that the directionality of emission from a cavity deformed from the circle can be enhanced in several times using relatively small deformations. However this is achieved at the expense of higher threshold values.

articleTitle: Simulation of propagation of modes in planar gradient-index hyperbolic secant waveguide
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We obtained expressions for TE and TM modes of the planar hyperbolic secant (HS) waveguide. We found waveguide parameters for which the fundamental mode has minimal width. By FDTD-simulation we show propagation of TE-modes and periodical reconstruction of non-modal fields in bounded HS-waveguides. We show that truncated HS-waveguide focuses plane wave into spot with diameter 0.132 of wavelength.

articleTitle: Study of dispersion and its relationship with power confinement in a single-mode optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Dispersion is one of the very important factors in the optical fibers that distort every limited bandwidth signals and cause problems for detecting the signal in the receiver. Therefore, prediction of dispersion value is inevitable. In this paper, the dispersion for an ideal optical fiber is simulated and calculated, and then the total dispersion and waveguide dispersion and their relationship with power confinement are studied.

articleTitle: Modeling of fluctuations of laser radiation scattered on the reflector array in a turbulent atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The method of inflammation early detection based on tracking of shift of diffraction pattern obtained by the laser radiation reflection from tetrahedral retro-reflectors array is described. The computer model of this method is developed. The simulation results show that with increasing magnitude of atmosphere turbulence there is an increase of the shift of diffraction pattern local maximum.

articleTitle: The conception of scales echeloning for precise optical indication of pressure and temperature
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: In this work, a gas-filled 1D elastic photonic crystal, sensitive to the external pressure and temperature, is considered as an optical indicator. Due to the well expressed identity of the bandgap structure behaviour an opportunity arises to unite several scales of pressure or temperature which may be organized on the same substrate. A general conception of scales echeloning based on sequential connection of scales during the measurement process is proposed. The scales echeloning for precise indication of pressure and temperature on the base of pneumatic photonic crystals is discussed. An eight digit accuracy measurement procedure based on a strip gas-filled photonic crystal for three laser wavelengths 0.488 μm, 0.694 μm and 1.065 μm is described.

articleTitle: Methods of distance errors compensation in dynamically changing conditions
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The analysis of measuring errors for the laser distance meter in dynamically changing conditions is carried out. Possibilities to compensate the measuring errors are considered. Efficiency of methods to increase the measuring accuracy is researched.

articleTitle: Radiation losses in planar dielectric waveguide with random rough surface
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The statistical model of light scattering by the rough surface of planar dielectric waveguide is developed, which is free from weakly guiding approximation. The dependence of loss on the refractive index difference, thickness of the waveguide core and correlation characteristics of the scattering surface is investigated.

articleTitle: Decelerating Airy pulses
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: It is shown that an electromagnetic wave equation in time domain is reduced in paraxial approximation to an equation similar to the Schrodinger equation but in which the time and space variables play opposite roles. This equation has solutions in form of time-varying pulses with the Airy function as an envelope. The pulses are generated by a source point with an Airy time varying field and propagate in vacuum preserving their shape and magnitude. The motion is according to a quadratic law with the velocity changing from infinity at the source point to zero in infinity. These one-dimensional results are extended to the 3D+time case when a similar Airy-Bessel pulse is excited by the field at a plane aperture. The same behaviour of the pulses, the non-diffractive preservation and their deceleration, is found.

articleTitle: On optical properties of holographic sensors based on silver emulsions
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Here we discuss optical properties of the holographic sensors - a new class of analytical optical devices. We discuss the issue of sensors operating mode choice of and the influence of their light-scattering properties. Ways to study the spatial uniformity of the holographic sensors are discussed.

articleTitle: Grid receiver for measuring of laser radiation characteristics
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Grids from thin metal wires are used for measurement of laser radiation characteristics. The device contains 4 grids with 8 nickel wires in each. The diameter of wires is 40 μm. The diameter of window is 60 mm. The algorithms of signal processing for measuring of radiation intensity distribution, coordinates of energetic center, diameter of beam, direction of polarization are given.

articleTitle: Thermocapillary effects in CO2 laser cutting of metals
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The measurements of local pulsations of brightness temperature T of melt radiance along the front of the cut of metal sheet by CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser are carried out. Both spectrum regions of hydrodynamic and capillary turbulence of temperature fluctuations are shown with experimental estimation of threshold of thermocapillary effect of absorption as 1 MW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Theoretical study of plasmon resonances in linear chain of silver nanowires
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: In this paper we investigate the plasmon resonance coupling in linear chain of infinite silver nanowires. It was shown the dependence of the resonant peaks location and their magnitudes on the illumination direction and on the distance between the nanowires. The Mie series expansion is used to derive the solution.

articleTitle: General astigmatic nonparaxial wave beams and packets
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We show that any solution of the paraxial parabolic equation can be simply transformed to some nonharmonic in time exact solution of the wave equation. On the basis of this observation, we generalize the known Bateman-type waves and present a family of exact solutions of the wave equation involving an arbitrary function, waveform. Argument of this function is much similar to that which appear in general astigmatic paraxial Gaussian beam. Special choices of the waveform allow general astigmatic beam-like and packetlike waves with Gaussian-type localization in space and time.

articleTitle: Sensor device structures based on thick-film ceramic materials
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Sensor device multifunctional temperature/humidity sensitive thick-film structures based on spinel-type semiconducting and insulating ceramics of different chemical composition Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> (with p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> -type of electrical conductivity), Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">08</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> (with p-type of electrical conductivity) and magnesium aluminate i-type MgAl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> ceramics were fabricated and investigated. These sensor elements are shown to be successfully applied for integrated environmental sensors.

articleTitle: Multistable response of trapping light nonlinear structures
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We present our recent results related to effects of bistability, multistability, and nonreciprocity in a finite layered photonic band-gap chiral structure with an asymmetrically introduced nonlinear defect and in a very thin planar meta-material consisted of a peculiar patterned metal layer placed on a nonlinear substrate. Remarkable feature of both kinds of these structures is a bearing of a strong localized high-intensity electromagnetic field. We argue that an application of this so-called trapped mode resonance operation is a promising technique to design all-optical control devices.

articleTitle: Spiral beams: The results and outlook
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The structurally stable light fields with rotation under propagation is considered. Some examples of practical applications are shown.

articleTitle: The spectral characteristics of lasing of the planar structures of cholesteric liquid crystals and their dependence on the nature and quality of textures
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Influence of quality of a planar structure in cholesteric liquid crystals (CLC) different type on their lasing spectra is investigated. It is established that in steroidal CLC decrease in quality of a structure leads to shift of lasing spectrum from the center to edge the selective reflection (SR) band. In induced CLC at similar changes the lasing spectrum appears mainly on its edge.

articleTitle: Holographic sensors
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The holographic sensor is actually a thick hologram plane mirror about the size of a square centimeter. By placing such plate in a special cell containing 24 cells of 2 mm diameter each of which contains 50 ul of fluid being analyzed, we can create chips for the simultaneous determination of several tens of samples.

articleTitle: Mid-infrared pulsed radiation in a dual-wavelength vertical external cavity surface-emitting laser
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Parameters of mid-infrared pulsed radiation (~17.1 μm) being emitted due to intracavity nonlinear optical frequency conversion in the dual-wavelength vertical external-cavity surface-emitting laser are analyzed. Nonlinear optical frequency conversion is supposed to be realized in the quasi-phase-matched crystal. The dependence of peak pulse power at the wavelength corresponding to the mid-infrared range on the nonlinear crystal length at various values of a loss factor is obtained.

articleTitle: Biophotonics of new optical method of regulating oxygen concentration in biological tissue
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Biophotonics of laser-tissue interaction at low intensity laser radiation on blood oxyhemoglobin is the interesting field of modern photomedicine and photobiology. The results in vivo investigations of laser-induced photodissosiation of oxyhemoglobin in cutaneous blood vessels and its role in biomedical processes are presented. New optical technology for increasing the local oxygen concentration in biological tissue is developed.

articleTitle: Express-diagnostics of a crater growth on laser plasma materials processing
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Acoustic emission of a zone of the destruction formed during influence of pulse laser radiation on a surface of metal is considered. Dependence of the time form of acoustic fluctuations on parameters of an irradiated material and the law of increase in depth of a crater was estimated. It is revealed, that at action on a surface of the copper sample of a laser impulse duration ~20 μc time of growth of a zone of destruction makes approximately 40 MKC, that will well be coordinated with time of existence of plasma formation at a surface of the target exposed to laser-plasma processing (~50 μc).

articleTitle: Modeling of XeCl excilamps on binary mixtures in mono-pulse regime of work
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The results of modeling at use Cl2:Xe binary mixes at total pressure 10 Torr are considered. The basic channel of XeCl-molecules formation is harpoon reaction. Excilamp efficiency can reach 20 % at use of small values of storage capacity and areas discharge S>;2,5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and at that pullse energy is equal 0,017 J.

articleTitle: Changes in output characteristics of broad-band superluminescent diodes in the process of long-term operation
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Methods and results of reliability tests of SQW broad-band superluminescent diodes (SLD-37 series), widely used in optical coherence tomography (OCT) are presented. Main attention was paid to the alteration of SLD spectral characteristics in the aging process. It is shown that the usage of these methods in the input control of processed epiwafers deployed in the production of active elements for SLD-modules ensures the estimation of their expected life time (MTTF).

articleTitle: Laser-microwave spectroscopy of Ag I atoms in F Rydberg state
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: For the first time the energy level positions of Ag I atoms have been measured with high accuracy by means of laser-microwave spectroscopy in the 149-289 GHz frequency range. The new measurements cover the range of principal quantum number n=28-38 for Rydberg series F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2,7/2</sub>. Using our measured frequencies the quantum defect constants for this series are obtained. The description of our spectrometer, measurement technique and results are presented.

articleTitle: On a new type electrically pumped lasers with impact excitation mechanism
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Necessity for a new type electrically pumped lasers with the impact excitation mechanism in the case of materials activated with transition metals and rare-earths is considered. It is shown that such lasers can be only realized on the basis of thin-film MISIM structures (M is a electrode, I is an insulator layer and S is a semiconductor electroluminescent film), which are optical planar waveguide. The possibility of creation the new laser is demonstrated by obtaining the stimulated emission and the laser oscillation in thin-film waveguide ZnS:Cr structures.

articleTitle: The XeCl laser with the adjustable shape and duration of generation pulse
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The generation parameters of LC-contour excitation system are studied for electro-discharge excimer XeCl laser using a Ne-Xe-HCl mixture. A computation model is developed for finding the generation parameters. It is shown that generation of short radiation pulses and relatively long pulses is possible due to changing of LC- contour parameters.

articleTitle: Magnetooptic polariton spectra in nonlinear magnetogyrotropic medium
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Spectra of magnetooptical polaritons in nonlinear magnetogyrotropic medium at presence of magnetostatic field are received. Nonlinear internal ion polarization arisen under the influence of high-frequency electromagnetic field is taken into account. The polariton spectra subjected to strength and direction of the external magnetostatic field are calculated.

articleTitle: Contrastivity of complicated structures: 1D photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: A novel definition of optical contrastivity for complicated structures as relative total gap taken over a chosen range of frequencies is introduced. The notion introduced for ordered 1D systems retains its meaning for 2D, 3D and disordered structures. The contrast sensibility to parameters is analyzed for a wide area.

articleTitle: Loop effect on Long-Period Fiber Gratings produced by electric arc
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: This article presents the fabrication of Long Period Gratings in Optical Fiber (LPFGs) applied to the sensing loops. In implementing the manufacturing method used a commercial splicer fiber optic (FiTel S-175), capable of being programmed to a short section of standard optical fiber (SMF28) is taken at intervals between shots in a range from 400μm to of 650μm. The LPFGs Being able to obtain through attenuation bands above 20 dB, while the wavelength of central attenuation is close to 1550nm. We shows the experimental scheme to measure curvatures with diameters ranging between 12 and 13.1cm, having a linear variation of peak output cut at the LPFGs with tuning of 17nm.

articleTitle: Radiation spectrum of electrons moving in spiral in transparent medium
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The structure of the spectral distribution of the time-averaged radiation power of system of electrons moving one by one along the spiral in transparent medium is studied in relativistic case. The hopping variation in synchrotron-Cherenkov radiation spectrum of one and two electrons moving in spiral conditioned by anomalous Doppler effect is investigated.

articleTitle: A numerical method for analysis of waveguide-separated absorption charge multiplication-avalanche photodetector(WG-SACM-APD)
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: In this paper a numerical method for analysis of waveguide-separated absorption charge multiplication avalanche photodetector (WG-SACM-APD) is presented. Considering the theory of Taylor series, frequency domain modeling of this detector including parasitic sources is achieved. Finally, the detector's transfer function and bandwidth with respect to the multiplication gain are also investigated.

articleTitle: Heating processes in cw four-level microlasers and their influence on the parameters of the laser mode
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The heat processes are considered for continuous wave GGG:Nd, YAP:Nd, YVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>:Nd and YAG:Nd microlasers. The distribution of the temperature as well as the thermo-induced changes of the refraction index and the deformations is determined. At the given distributions of the refractive index and the deformations the components of (ABCD) - matrix, the laser beam waist and the divergence are determined in the wide range of the values of the pumping beam power and radius, the heat transfer coefficient and the geometrical sizes of the active element.

articleTitle: Selection of the lasing frequency and heating the quantum-well heterostructure laser diodes
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Numerical simulation of controlling the lasing frequency for the 1.5 μm-range quantum-well heterostructure laser diodes is developed with taking into account increasing the active region temperature under pump current modulation. Peculiarities of the amplitude-frequency characteristics are analyzed at selection of the lasing frequency. General description of the heating of the laser active region during the current modulation is given and selection conditions of the lasing frequency that provide the response bandwidth up to 40 GHz are established.

articleTitle: Development of wavefront sensors for IR-radiation
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: In this paper we propose two types of Hartmann wavefront sensors for registration of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser radiation. One type is based on uncooled bolometric camera and another is based on thermoelectric quadrant sensors. The results of sensors testing are represented in the paper. Their main specification, including accuracy and dynamic range are given also. For example, for a wide aperture beam, 150 mm, the dynamic range of measured wavefront aberrations for thermoelectric quadrant sensor was about 375 microns (tilts). These sensors could be built-in into the adaptive optics systems to correct for infrared radiation.

articleTitle: System of multifrequency terahertz laser's cavity tuning
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Frequency tuning of the terahertz laser's cavity technique is presented. The method allows setting of needed frequency shift (relative to a laser active medium central line lasing) value, without using of the frequency measurement equipment. Compound terahertz cavity scheme is proposed, which makes possible instantaneous choosing of several fixed frequencies within laser active material lasing line. Frequency stabilizing of the operating channels tuning provided by a control channel in the compound cavity.

articleTitle: Application of Fourier transforms to find propagation constants of the localized modes symmetric planar waveguides. Analogies in the quantum mechanics
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Numerical method of finding propagation constants of the localized modes of symmetric planar waveguides and solution of the stationary Schrödinger equation is developed. The method is based on Fourier transform of the wave equation and as result is obtained an integral equation in which the integral is replaced by summation. In of the final case, we obtain of linear algebra problem on the eigenvalues and eigenvectors. The method is tested on many examples.

articleTitle: Simulation of intensity of single-mode Photonic Crystal Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: In this paper shown that absorbed pump intensity and amplified signal intensity of single-mode Photonic Crystal Fiber Laser are about approximation 10 times more than absorbed pump intensity and amplified signal intensity of single-mode of Fiber Laser.

articleTitle: Application of three-mirror laser resonator in two-wavelength interferometer scheme
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The two-wavelength generation in He-Ne laser resonator has been used for the interferometric measurements of displacements and strains. The oscillations on 0,63 and 3,39 microns are simultaneously realized and investigated. The precise multi-channel temperature meter with resolution of 0,001 K in the 273-378 K range was applied for temperature monitoring of the laser. The interferometric schemes are based on a three-mirror laser resonator using a principle of an optical feedback. The interferometer length was ranged from a few meters up to 300 meters in our experiments. Fabrication of a dispersion interferometer - refractometer, which corrects of a refractive index along the extended measuring baseline, is possible with this technique application.

articleTitle: Plasmon-assisted scattering of light by a discrete corner made of silver nanowires
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We consider the problem of the H-polarized plane wave scattering by a discrete comer made of circular wires, using the field expansions in local coordinates and addition theorems for cylindrical functions. The scattering cross-sections and near-field patterns are found numerically and plasmon and grating-type resonances are studied for the corners of nano-size silver wires.

articleTitle: Compact-sized excimer laser with two-sides preionization
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Compact-sized monopulse excimer laser with foot-print equal to only 250×80 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, total height 250 mm and beam axis height 50 mm was designed. Output energy at wavelength 308 nm (XeCl* mixture) is 5 mJ, maximal repetition rate - 1-2 pulses per second, beam divergence - 8 miliradians. Such small foot-print, small axis height of beam in combination with low weight of laser (5 kg) allow them to be used in various optical schemes, where traditional, typical bulky ecximer lasers are unapplicable. Moreover, small dimensions, low weight in combination with low energy consumption (a few Wts) allow them to be used in clear “field” conditions. Beside abovementioned designed laser differs from traditional ones by two-sides preionization: “spark” near “hot” massive electrode and so called “capacitive” or “barrier” under ground grid one. Such a two-sides preionization provides both igniting and sustaining of wider discharge thus allowing to reach beam with higher simmetry - its cross-section is 15×20 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Kinetics of thermally induced transformation of free radicals AsO44− → AsO32− in KDP single crystals
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: ESR study of the thermally induced transformation of impurity arsenic-containing free radicals produced by γ-rays in KDP single crystals is carried out at 100-150 °C. It is established that the transformation occurs in accordance with the second order kinetics reaction. The activation energy of the transformation is determined.

articleTitle: Reduce of electrical power loss in three Terminal vertical cavity surface emitting laser
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: This study shows that by increasing current path inside of VCSEL, heat loss will be decreased, which results in increasing the wavelength stability. An alternative and significant advantage of the proposed method is that in mass production process it has in compatibility with the general mass production technology of commercial VCSELs. The simulation performance indicates that heat loss in three Terminal VCSEL is comparatively decreased in comparison with conventional VCSELs, consequently increasing the stability of work wavelength of VCSEL.

articleTitle: Switching dynamics of the wideband PhC-based filter with Kerr saturable nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: In the paper, we investigate in details switching ON and switching OFF dynamics of the wideband optical filter on the basis of nonlinear photonic crystal which possess all-optical bistability properties. The all-optical flip-flop using ultra-short pulses with duration lower than 200 fs have been demonstrated in such filters.

articleTitle: Differential electroabsorption spectra of InGaN/GaN QWs with indium surface segregation
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: In this work, we investigate the influence of the indium surface segregation on the differential absorption observed for different inverse biases applied to the structure. Obtained results evidence that the indium surface segregation leads to more sharp dependence of the absorption on the applied bias for a wide frequency range above the red edge. This feature can be used for experimental measurements of the segregation lengths applying optical spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Numerical analyses of water media with laser fluorescence method
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Nowadays, the spectral optic methods for discovering and studying mineral oils in the water are widely applied to and their principle advantage towards other methods is their express-diagnostics and remote sounding. The express-diagnostics implies the rapid discovery of water pollution using optic methods in order to eliminate and liquidate pollution sources on time (tankers, terminals etc). The difference is even between optic methods. One of them is the method of laser fluorescence. There are lots of organic compounds in the nature exposing special characteristics after optical excitation, they start radiating - fluorescence. These organic compounds are divided into four classes, they are: 1) photosynthetic substances - phytoplanktons; 2) amino acids; 3) humus substances of water; 4) oil and mineral oils. So, it's doubtless that there are soluble organic fluorescent substances in water media. Their signal of fluorescence creates a background on the signal of oil fluorescence and hampers the progress of oil discoveries. The fluorescence spectrums are created simultaneously and they represent the spectrums of signals created from both, oil and organic compounds. There are different ways of separating these spectrums, but none of them is absolute. That is why, it is necessary to study and investigate the spectrums of fluorescence of organic compounds besides oil and mineral oils. It is comparatively simple to discover solid elements floating into the water and to define their concentration.

articleTitle: Simulation and optimization interaction of the laser radiation with the biotissues
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The mathematical model and software interaction of the laser radiation with the mediums is proposed. Software has been developed on basis of Monte-Carlo method. The heterogeneous properties of the medium, features of the absorption and scattering in individual layers are taken in account in calculations. Simulation distribution of the temperature in skin layers having vascular pathology under the action of laser radiation has been conducted. The parameters of the laser radiation and modes surface cooling of skin are optimized to achievement of required temperature in layer vascular pathology and prevention of the destruction in surface layers.

articleTitle: Coherent electron transport in single-molecular junction
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We have realized computing and analysis current-voltage characteristic. For this purpose we use transfer matrix method combined with Liouville-fon-Neymann equation. Obtained system of ordinary differentional equations describes time dependent changes of transition probabilities and concentrations in single-molecular junction. System was solved using Runge-Kutta method and time dependent polarization and concentration characteristics were obtained as a result.

articleTitle: Generation of the directed X-ray radiation at mechanoluminescence
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Results of the experimental investigations of the powerful pulsed laser radiation interaction with three-dimensional photonic structures (synthetic opal matrixes) are presented. Simultaneously with visible range luminescence X-ray generation was registered. Possible mechanisms responsible for X-ray generation are being discussed.

articleTitle: Maximum reflection and minimum transmission of electromagnetic waves by negative permeability-ferrite waveguide
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: A magnetized ferrite waveguide situated between two half free spaces is investigated theoretically. Maxwell's equations and Snell's law are used to calculate the reflected and transmitted powers of the structure numerically. It is demonstrated that, maximum reflectance and minimum transmittance can be obtained by tuning the applied magnetic field.

articleTitle: Ultrashort optical interconnections of peripheral devices for next generation data processing systems
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We present a theoretical and experimental analysis on the static and modulation characteristics of components for 10 Gb/s ultrashort optical interconnects. Numerical analysis of geometrical parameters for optical light source and detector shows optimal values where bandwidth is maximal. Intracavity-contacted oxide confined vertical cavity surface emitted lasers and resonant cavity enhanced photodiode are presented as good choice for next generation high-speed optical interconnects.

articleTitle: Multichannel fiber optic recirculating memory
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The structure of the optoelectronic dynamic memory. based on a method of regenerative storage and record of the optical information in a recirculating memory element with a fiber-optical delay line is offered, the multiparameter analysis of information characteristics of such system is lead.

articleTitle: Control of the chromatic dispersion of photonic crystal fibers for supercontinuum and photon pairs generation
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The interplay between chromatic dispersion and nonlinear effects is crucial for an efficient exploitation of non linear propagation in photonic crystal fibers (PCF). Once a PCF preform has been prepared, changing the parameters that control the fabrication process it is possible to adjust the dispersion properties of the fiber. In addition, it is particularly useful to develop postprocessing techniques that enable a fine adjustment of the dispersion along a section of PCF. The tapering of PCF, using a fusion and pulling technique, has been established as a rather useful technique to engineer the dispersion properties along tens of centimeters. Some of our recent experiments demonstrate that the use of erbium doped PCF enables an optical control of the dispersion through optical pumping of the rare earth ions. Since our interest is focused on the development of fiber light sources, we will present several experiments on supercontinuum and photon pairs generation, through degenerate four-wave mixing (FWM), in order to illustrate the control that one can achieve on the optical spectra of these light sources by tailoring the dispersion of the fibers.

articleTitle: Estimation of linear polarization angle of laser radiation with two-grating thin-wire bolometer
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The measuring method of linear polarization of laser radiation with two bolometric gratings with no mutually perpendicular directions of bolometric elements has been confirmed experimentally.

articleTitle: Optical fractals: Characterization, cavities, coherence and connections
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Uniform and regular systems can generate optical fractals. After characterizing different fractal-generating systems, emphasis is placed on the roles of boundary conditions and cavity feedback. New aspects of linear and nonlinear optical fractals are presented, along with considerations of system coherence and novel connections to some classic systems and configurations.

articleTitle: High resolution sub-Doppler laser FM-spectroscopy of molecular iodine vapor
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We apply the self-calibrated sub-Doppler laser FM-spectroscopy to the study of hyperfine structure of molecular iodine. The ability of proposed technique to the high accurate measurements of iodine hyperfine structure in wide region of mode-hope free tuning of diode laser is demonstrated. The nonlinear absorption spectra of molecular iodine embedded into the pores of synthetic opal are studied with sub-megahertz resolution.

articleTitle: Surface plasmon polariton waves in optically active media
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We investigate surface plasmon polariton waves on the semi-infinite and multilayered interfaces of metals or metamaterials with optically active dielectrics. Such surface waves consist of two partial components with different polarization and localization. Propagation constant, localization coefficients and polarization of surface waves were calculated in the linear approximation that can be used in the cases of weak gyrotropy. Plasmon polariton waves on the interfaces with stronger gyrotropy were investigated numerically. We found out that there is a critical value of gyrotropic coefficient above which there are no localized surface waves on the interface.

articleTitle: Anisotropic effect and negative dielectric permittivity in crystals
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Anisotropy effects on the negative dielectric permittivity (DP) formation in the frequency region near the phonon lattice vibrations are considered using three crystalline modifications of boron nitride. Quantitative data on frequency intervals and negative DP values are presented for all anisotropic modifications. It is shown that anomalous dispersion of the refractive index falls to 0 <; n <; 1 in the presence of negative DP, but always leaves n >; 1 in the absence of negative DP. The significant role of the polar vibrations damping to determination of the real limits of negative DP region is clarified, especially for crystals with symmetry lower than cubic.

articleTitle: Atomic soliton lasers and potential applications
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Atomic soliton lasers are coherent matter-wave emitters that produce localized pulses of atoms that are extracted from an ultracold atomic reservoir. In adequate conditions it is possible to obtain matter-wave soliton trains that propagate undistorted, a property that makes them very useful for ultra-sensitive measurements like gravity-waves detection or atomic interferometry. Some new applications and results will we presented.

articleTitle: Self-mixing interferometry: A universal yardstick to measure almost everything
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Self-mixing interferometry (SMI) is a new scheme of interferometry having several advantages compared to standard configurations: it can work with no optical part external to the laser, is self-aligned, is immune to external stray light, and can measure also on target with diffusing surfaces. In this paper, an overview of the several measurements already demonstrated with self-mixing is presented, with application the measurements of kinematic quantities (displacement, vibration. etc.) as well physical (linewidth, alfa factor, etc).

articleTitle: Features of optical spectral-selective elements characteristics with the increased value of refraction index
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: In report modeling of characteristics of optical spectral-selective elements of the cylindrical form with the increased value of the refraction index, using effect of light scattering is organized. As have shown results of researches, application of cylindrical optical element for spectral angular selection is limited. At increase in value of refraction index the optical element starts to function in a mode of quasi uniform light scattering.

articleTitle: Spatio-temporal carrier dynamics of a dualwavelength vertical external cavity surface-emitting laser
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The mathematical model of a dual-wavelength emission from a vertical external cavity surface-emitting laser taking into account the transverse distribution both of optical fields and pump carrier flux density is built. Spatio-temporal dynamics of charge carriers and photons is analyzed. It is shown that the most pronounced optical hole-burning can be observed near the optical axis of the laser.

articleTitle: Modelling the processes of Relaxed Optics in the regime of saturation the excitation: Structural approach
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The problem of modeling processes of Relaxed Optics (RO) in the regime of saturation the excitation for the silicon and germanium is discussed. Correlations between photoinized, plasmic and thermal processes are analyzed for various regimes of irradiation. The problems of creation stable and metastable structures and phase transformations are discussed too.

articleTitle: Performance of phase-modulated microwave photonics in the presence of group delay and reflection amplitude ripples of the dispersive device
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We develop an analytic approach to investigate the effect of reflection amplitude and group delay ripples of the dispersive device on the performance of phase-modulated microwave-photonic filters. Experimental results conform to our proposed analytical approach.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis of laser radiation transmission at interface between two quasi-crystalline layers of the retina
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Theoretical analysis of the laser radiation transmission at interface between the quasi-crystalline layers of the retina (a layer of nerve fibers and photoreceptor disks) is analyzed in a frame of holographic model of physiological optics. To solve the problem, we have obtained analogues of Fresnel's formulas for the interface between two uniaxial crystals. The results may be applied for diagnosis and treatment of ophthalmologic diseases by laser techniques.

articleTitle: Modeling of XeCl excilamps in pulse-periodic mode of work
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Model of XeCl excilamp taking into account process of Cl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> regeneration is developed. On this basis it is shown, that power of radiation XeCl excilamp in pulse-periodic operating mode can reach several kilowatts at efficiency ~20 % at use of binary mixes (Xe and Cl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) at total pressure 10 Torr.

articleTitle: Modelling the processes of relaxed optics in the regime of saturation the excitation: Structural approach
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The problem of modeling processes of Relaxed Optics (RO) in the regime of saturation the excitation for the silicon and germanium is discussed. Correlations between photoinized, plasmic and thermal processes are analyzed for various regimes of irradiation. The problems of creation stable and metastable structures and phase transformations are discussed too.

articleTitle: Optical properties of II-Mn-VI films obtained by close-spaced vacuum sublimation technique
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Optical properties of Zn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>S and Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Te films, obtained by close-spaced vacuum sublimation technique are investigated. Measuring of optical characteristics layers was carried out by spectrophotometric analysis. This research allowed to obtained spectral distributions of transmittance, reflectance and absorption coefficients of films and to expect band-gap energy of materials.

articleTitle: Specific spatial domain of a random laser
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Dependencies of random lasing (RL) spectrum parameters on crosswise dimension of active region and thickness of multiply scattering active medium were experimentally investigated. These dependencies reveal characteristic points caused by specific spatial domains of RL: RL radiation confinement, active region and RL mode localization. The dependencies allow finding the domain sizes.

articleTitle: Waveguide periodic structures induced by purple semiconductor laser in AgCl-Ag films
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Periodic structures are obtained under action of linearly polarized laser beam (407 nm) on AgCl-Ag films. Linear dichroism is observed in film absorption spectra. For the first time dichroism found to survive chemical removal of AgCl. Dichroism is explained by anisotropy of light absorption by Ag particles in grooves.

articleTitle: Solvent effect on characteristics of tunable dye-mixture laser
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Spectral and energy characteristics of two red laser dyes and its mixtures in some solvents have been studied for the purpose to extend its tuning range throughout the red spectral region. The selected couple of the dyes have the absorption spectra in the close spectral regions near wavelength of pumping, but its fluorescence spectra have essentially different Stokes shift. Influence of the dye concentration and solvents effect on the output energy lasing in non-selective cavity and tuning range of the mixture in the cavity with diffraction grating have been studded and analyzed.

articleTitle: Recording/reading features of reflective holographic gratings on photopolymers with real time response
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Application of tilted holographic photopolymer Bragg gratings in the capacity of reflective gratings is considered theoretically. The negative appearances caused by a volume shrink-age of medium and changes of an average refractive index were taken into account. It is offered two different ways of recording/reading similar reflective gratings over the range 300-1000 nm that matches to the transparence spectrum of a used photopolymer material.

articleTitle: Invisibility cloak with use non-singular coordinate transformation
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Non-singular coordinate transformation is investigated and expressions for a component of permittivity and permeability are received. Numerical modelling of the corresponding device of invisibility is lead. It is shown that the total size of scattering from the invisibility device in a for zone corresponds to size of scattering from the perfect electric conductor cylinder which is “base” of coordinate transformation.

articleTitle: The postoperative rehabilitation of the autoimmune thyroiditis patients with the use of low-intensive laser therapy
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Was studied the clinical and hormonal status at patients with autoimmune thyroiditis on the therapy of low-intensive laser in 2 years after operation on a thyroid. The low-intensive laser therapy was high efficiency at the patients with autoimmune thyroiditis. Positive clinical effect was confirmed the normalization of hormonal thyroid status, to lower indexes of antithyroid auto antibodies and to normalize the cellular parameters of immunodefense.

articleTitle: Optical properties of the Ag and Au nanowires gratings
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We have studied surface plasmon modes on silver and gold nanowires of the fixed cross section. The spectral position of the plasmon resonance can be tuned by the appropriate choice of the nanowire geometry and material.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional simulation of a device to input light in a planar waveguide
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Using the FullWAVE software (www rsoftdesigii.com) that implements the finite-difference FDTD-method of solving Maxwell's equations, we simulate the performance of a three-dimensional nanophotonics device comprising a subwavelength diffraction grating, a wide and a narrow planar waveguide, and a photonic crystal (PhC) Mikaelian lens located in a thin silicon film coated on a substrate containing a three-period Bragg mirror.

articleTitle: Metallic waveguide cavity with a spherical mirror
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The influence of the curvature of the spherical mirror for metallic waveguide resonator of submillimeter laser (λ = 0.4326 mm) on energy losses and the mode composition of radiation is investigated. It is shown that the presence of quadratic phase aberrations in the mirrors of the waveguide cavity with an increase of its Fresnel number at monotonically decreasing of the energy losses for fundamental asymmetric mode TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11q</sub> due to a decrease of waveguide losses also leads to their substantial non-periodic oscillation.

articleTitle: Incident angle-dependent spectra of an anisotropic optical microcavity
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We simulate spectra of the optical microcavity based on a composite (mesoporous silicon)/(nematic liquid crystal). The incident angle-dependent calculations predict the transmission peak blueshift and splitting of transverse electric and transverse magnetic polarized modes due to birefringence of both porous host material and the anisotropic filler.

articleTitle: Surface plasmon resonances and gap size effects in multistrip nanoantennas
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We analyze numerically the light scattering and absorption by an ensemble of finite number of coplanar thin strips as a nanoantenna. The nature of associated surface-plasmon resonances in the optical band and the gap size effects arc investigated.

articleTitle: Adaptive photo-EMF detectors based on CdTe and their solid solutions
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The complex measurements of V(Ti)-doped CdTe (crystals and films) and their solid solutions were carried out. This allowed to establish the nature and energy structure of the intrinsic defects and impurity centers and to propose the micromechsnism of photo-EMF effect. The adaptive photodetectors based on these crystals and CdTe polycrystalline films were developed.

articleTitle: Impact of geometrical behaviors on operation parameters of a microstructured optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We investigated the impact of geometrical behaviors on operation parameters in the case of microstructured optical fiber with a ring of air holes. The found results show that at any of considered types defects mode field will have two pronounced maximums. We also have shown that random variations of inclusions diameter can increase total mode field power.

articleTitle: Slow-wave regimes of the photonic crystal waveguides
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Modified photonic crystal waveguides that support slow waves are considered. MIT Photonic-Band package is used for calculation of dispersion characteristics and electric field spatial distributions. Symmetrical and antisymmetrical guided modes with different phase velocities are obtained within and outside the photonic band gaps.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional multilayer mirrors for 60-GHz-band
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We have investigated numerically properties of periodic multilayer mirrors for 60-GHz wireless telecommunication band. It was shown that a quarter-wave mirror based on the crystalline quartz and high-permittivity ceramic (CeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) can provide high reflectivity within the whole 60-GHz band independently of the incident angle.

articleTitle: Error definition for nanoparticles size in liquid measured by correlation spectroscopy method
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Errors for nanoparticles size measurement in mono-disperse liquid media are determined by mathematical modeling. To reduce the errors of radii measurements in the range of 1 - 6 nm one-bit quantization method use is proposed.

articleTitle: Influence of substrate on temperature distribution in nitride laser diodes
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: In this work, we investigate the influence of the substrate material on the temperature distribution in the active region of the nitride-based quantum well UV light-emitting diodes. Results of mathematical modeling show that the application of the GaN substrate leads to a reduction of the averaged temperature in the active region of a few tens of degrees Kelvin comparing with the sapphire substrate.

articleTitle: Dilute nitride band engineering: A tool for intersubband gain without population inversion
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Interconduction band gain without global inversion is obtained by engineering conduction band dispersion relations with dilute N resonant centres. We recover the expected dispersive gain shape for similar masses and contrasting results if the effective masses characterizing the relevant subbands are very different.

articleTitle: Influence of thermal processes on the electron temperature in the active media of gas-discharge lasers
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: It was shown that in estimation of the electron temperature value in the gas-discharge positive column on the basis of the Schottky's relation, it is necessary to include not only pressure reduced value p<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, but to account for the discharge system structure and the thermal regime of the whole discharge system during the discharge.

articleTitle: Transient mode beating in disk microresonator at picosecond pulse excitation
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Transient pulse travelling inside circular microcavity has been studied theoretically using developed rigorous and efficient mathematical method. This method allows us to obtain analytical solution of the wave equation in the Laplace domain. Inverse transformation is obtained through evaluation of residues at singular points that represent excited modes of a resonator. External beam excitation is modelled by the point source with complex coordinates. Transient mode beating has been investigated and visualized.

articleTitle: Liquid cry stall dye doped distributed feedback lasing: Short prehistory and modern development
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The review of author's contributions on laser oscillation of structures with the static and induced phase Bragg grating in the planar oriented dye doped liquid crystal is made. Mode lasing spectra of the dye doped cholesteric liquid crystals (ChLC) are interpreted within the frames of the distributed feedback theory based on the coupled wave model of Shank-Kogelnik. Perspectivity of lasing with light induced Bragg gratings in nematic liquid crystals (NLC), including possibility of electrical frequency tuning of lasing due to NLC director reorientation is underlined.

articleTitle: Influence of the strong pulsed laser field at the resonant effects of quantum electrodynamics
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: The review on the resonant processes of quantum electrodynamics (QED) proceeding in the strong pulsed light fields, realised in modern powerful pulsed lasers is presented. The appearance of resonances in a laser field is one of the fundamental problems of QED in electromagnetic fields. Following QED processes of the second order in the fine structure constant in the pulsed laser field are considered: resonant spontaneous bremsstrahlung by an election scattered by a nucleus, resonant photocreation of electron-positron pairs on a nucleus, and resonant scattering of a lepton by a lepton. The resonant peak's altitude and width are defined by the external pulsed wave properties. It is demonstrated that the resonant cross sections may be several orders of magnitude greater than the corresponding cross sections in the absence of an external field. Results obtained may be experimentally verified, for example, by the scientific facilities at the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory and FAIR (Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research, Darmstadt. Germany).

articleTitle: High-order micro-ring resonator transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We present recent results on high-order micro-ring resonator transmission lines for photonic signal processing. These include the analysis of newly put forward structures for the control of the group delay and the realization of transmission filters.

articleTitle: An optical resonator with back deformable mirror for formation of a beam with preassigned intensity distribution
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: Presented are results of theoretical investigation of field formation with given intensity distribution for a resonator with back deformable mirror. Herewith the preassigned intensity distribution is fundamental mode; selectivity (with respect to losses for transverse modes) of a resonator with deformable mirror is comparable with selectivity of reference cavity.

articleTitle: Fabry-Perot surface plasmon polaritons in metal-dielectric gratings
publicationTitle: 2011 11th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (LFNM)
abstract: We investigate surface plasmon polaritons of Fabry-Perot type in periodic metal-dieleetric gratings. They originate in addition to conventional Bloch plasmons only if the slit walls are covered with metal. The analytical models for both vertical and horizontal Fabry-Perot plasmons are developed and they demonstrate qualitative agreement with results of numerical simulations. The corresponding resonance wavelengths are shown to be very sensitive to metal walls thickness.
